title: Cannabis use and memory function in humans
question: In humans, is cannabis use — whether acute administration, chronic/regular use, or medicinal THC/CBD formulations — associated with changes in memory function (working memory, verbal or episodic memory, or memory consolidation), as measured by validated neuropsychological tests or neuroimaging in experimental, observational, or longitudinal studies?

pico.population: Humans of any age — healthy volunteers or clinical/patient samples
pico.exposure: Cannabis or a defined cannabinoid: acute administration (THC/CBD challenge, smoked/vaporized/oral), chronic or regular recreational use, or a medicinal THC/CBD formulation (nabiximols, dronabinol, prescribed cannabis)
pico.comparator: Non-users, placebo, or the participants' own pre-exposure / baseline
pico.outcome: Memory function — working memory, verbal memory, episodic memory, or memory consolidation — measured with a validated neuropsychological test or with neuroimaging of a memory process

inclusion_criteria: Human participants (not animal, not in-vitro / cell work)
A cannabis or cannabinoid exposure is characterized (acute administration, chronic/regular use, or medicinal THC/CBD)
A memory outcome (working, verbal, episodic, or consolidation) is measured with a validated neuropsychological test or neuroimaging
Primary empirical study (experimental, observational, or longitudinal) — not a review, meta-analysis, commentary, or protocol

fields.label: Sample
fields.help: population studied: healthy adults, adolescents, patients, chronic users, etc.

fields.label: N
fields.help: number of participants in this arm/comparison

fields.label: Exposure
fields.help: acute administration, chronic/regular use, or medicinal THC/CBD

fields.label: Agent
fields.help: THC, CBD, THC:CBD, whole-plant/smoked, nabiximols, dronabinol, etc. (and dose if reported)

fields.label: Design
fields.help: e.g. double-blind RCT/crossover, cross-sectional, longitudinal cohort

fields.label: Measure
fields.help: validated test or neuroimaging paradigm (RAVLT, CVLT, n-back, digit span, fMRI encoding, etc.)

fields.label: Result
fields.help: the reported effect, with numbers/direction as stated
